data.name: Dorke and Ymp
data.detailed_description:
Dorke and Ymp is an unreleased Super Nintendo game developed back in the early 1990's by a Swedish company called Norse. The game was developed with unlicensed tools made by the game programmers. Unfortunately the game failed to acquire a publisher and was never released.

Luckily we found the original programmer, composer, and artist and we acquired the source code at about 50% of the game. We worked on the game for over a year to finally complete it.

This are the new features and updates done to the game:

•Over 100 Bugs and Crashing bugs fixed!
•Added a whole new world and levels (Volcano)
•Added Menu, cut-scenes and ending.
•Implemented password system
•Designed, developed and implemented boss fights (4) according to the original game story.
•Organized the game to be able to play with continuity.
•Over 40 levels and 10 hours of gameplay!

This game is a puzzle adventure platformer in which you got to help Dorke (and Ymp) to do some errands for your evil Master Wizard in exchange of training you and teaching you his magic spells.

The game is very very hard and challenging, but hardcore games will have fun playing it!

reviews.review:
I'm not going to lie, I had never heard of this game until I saw it in a Fanatical bundle and figured, "Why not?" Because it was so cheap. I'd like to recommend this game and say it's just "not for everyone" but decided after beating it that it was too annoying at times to deserve a recommendation. Instead, I'd like to say it's a light no, but you can think of it more as a mixed review.

The controls are clunky, which is fine because what else would you expect from a game that was originally supposed to be on the SNES? The art style/graphics are... fine, for the most part, but the first world is really visually and mechanically boring. The game really starts to feel, not good, but better once you get to the second world. The level design feels LESS random, and the worlds themselves actually look unique.

All of that considered, I WOULD have recommended the game, but then I spent about two hours on World 4-8, and my thoughts changed because it highlights what are, in my opinion, two of the game's worst issues. Those issues being the game never explains anything and most of the levels feel randomly put together by a seven-year-old trying out Super Mario Maker for the first time. Good lord, I don't know what the developers were thinking with this level! I had to watch a walkthrough on YouTube, which I could only find one of, just to figure out how to traverse the level. To actually beat the level, you have to do what I assume is a bug several times. Whether it's a bug or an unexplained mechanic, it is too annoyingly hard to perform consistently.

Even though I'm only giving Dorke and Ymp a "light no," I would also like to mention what I liked about it. The controls are very clunky, but I found them kind of charming after a while and actually kind of like how shooting enemies works in theory. For the most part, you control Dorke, but to shoot and glide, you use Ymp. The shooting is comparable to having an arm on your back and throwing one of those rubber balls you got as a kid from one of those quarter machines at a grocery store. This sounds clunky/frustrating, and it kind of is (especially against the bees -_-), but I think it's the clunk that made it feel all the more satisfying near the middle of the game when I actually had the hang of it.

All in all, I don't regret getting and playing the game even if a lot of it was excrutiatingly annoying. If you're into these kinds of old-school clunky games and you can find a way to get it SUPER CHEAP, like I did, then yeah, it's probably worth a shot. Otherwise, you should probably pass on this one.
